subject: MAP: benchmarking scope + measured results for inference acceptance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@atlas.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — benchmarking scope and acceptance criteria

Emma —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our MAP we want to get a short, focused benchmarking run under the workload that most closely matches your production traffic so we can confirm performance acceptance before we finalize the Dedicated capacity pricing. I sketched a recommended scope below so we can align quickly.

Summary (ask): run a 1-hour sustained benchmark on your representative prompt set (we'll provide scripts) against the candidate model variant and capture TTFT, per-token latency, throughput, and error rate. Deliverables: 1) raw metrics CSV, 2) summarized PASS/FAIL vs MAP SLOs, 3) load generator config.

Proposed workload definition (brief):
- Prompt distribution: short 60% (<=64 tokens), medium 30% (64-512), long 10% (>512)
- Request rate: ramp to target over 5 minutes, then 55 minutes sustained
- Concurrency modes: steady 40 concurrent streams + burst test to 80 for 5 minutes
- Model: redwood/opt-13B-quant@v1 (we'll run a variant if you prefer)
- Tokenization: same tokenizer as production; include deterministic seed

Success criteria (MAP SLOs):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): 95th percentile < 300 ms
- Per-token latency: 95th percentile < 30 ms/token
- Aggregate throughput: sustained >= 1,000 tokens/sec
- Error/timeout rate: < 0.5%
- No service-level errors or repeated degraded responses during run

Logistics:
- We can run the test in your staging VPC or on Redwood Dedicated sandbox (your choice).
- Dates: can execute anytime between Mar 3–6; target to close acceptance by Mar 12 so procurement can finalize commit.
- I'll cc procurement once we lock the date.

Please confirm whether staging or Redwood sandbox is preferred, and attach the production prompt set you want us to use (or we can use the sample prompts we discussed).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma@atlas.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T02:12:00-07:00
Subject: Benchmark results (Atlas MAP) — run summary + raw CSV

Team / Emma —

We executed the run in Atlas staging (per Emma's request) using redwood-loadgen v0.9.1 and the prompt set Emma supplied. Attached are the raw CSV and the loadgen config. Below are the key metrics, followed by pass/fail vs the MAP SLOs and a brief notes section.

Test window: 2026-03-04T22:00:00Z to 2026-03-04T23:00:00Z
Model variant: redwood/opt-13B-quant@v1
Load harness: redwood-loadgen v0.9.1, batch_size dynamic (target 8), token sampling disabled (deterministic)
Prompts: representative_prompts_v2.json (60/30/10 short/medium/long)
Concurrency: steady 40 streams; burst to 80 for 5 minutes at minute 35

Aggregate results (sustained steady window):
- Median TTFT: 110 ms
- 95th TTFT: 220 ms
- Median per-token latency: 12 ms/token
- 95th per-token latency: 27.5 ms/token
- Sustained aggregate throughput: 1,450 tokens/sec
- Peak throughput (burst): 1,680 tokens/sec
- Error rate (timeouts / 5xx): 0.12%
- GPU utilization (avg across pool): 72%
- Memory headroom: ~2.1 GB per GPU on average

Pass/Fail vs MAP SLOs:
- TTFT 95th < 300 ms: PASS
- Per-token 95th < 30 ms/token: PASS (27.5 ms)<
- Aggregate throughput >= 1,000 tokens/sec: PASS (1,450 tokens/sec)
- Error rate < 0.5%: PASS (0.12%)

Notes and observations:
- Long prompts (the 10% bucket) contributed disproportionately to p95 latency but still within SLOs. If Atlas expects >20% long prompts in prod, we recommend a follow-up run with higher long-prompt ratio.
- The burst to 80 concurrent streams saw a transient dip in per-token tail latency (p95 increased to ~38 ms) but no functional errors and recovered within 90s. Consider soft throttling for burst windows if Atlas needs guaranteed p95 during bursts.
- We captured 10 sample outputs per prompt bucket and included them in the CSV for semantic review (column sample_output). No obvious truncation or artifacting observed.

Recommended next steps (MAP cadence):
1) Atlas to sign acceptance for performance based on these results.
2) Redwood to provision Dedicated sandbox for a 2-week pilot starting Mar 15 (option: earlier if procurement is ready).
3) If Atlas wants an expanded run (higher long-prompt percentage or longer duration), schedule that as an MAP extension.

Attachments: atlas_map_benchmark_results.csv (raw metrics, 42KB), loadgen_config.yml (test config, 3KB)

--
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Emma / procurement team —

Appreciate the speedy turnaround and for pulling the staging window together. Based on Rishi's run summary, Atlas meets the agreed MAP SLOs. From our side this clears the performance gate for finalizing the Dedicated commitment.

Operational items to close in the MAP:
- Procurement: please confirm the number of reserved GPU slots (baseline + burst) you want for contract pricing. Our recommended starter footprint based on the run is: 6 x A100-equivalent slots with autoscale to +50% for burst.
- Pilot dates: Redwood proposes Mar 15–Mar 29 (2-week pilot). We can accelerate if procurement signs before Mar 12.
- Telemetry: We'll enable MAP telemetry for the pilot (cost breakdown per-token, per-route latency, and alerting).

If procurement confirms slot counts and signs, I'll coordinate closing paperwork and our Dedicated ops team will provision the pilot environment.

Next call: propose Mar 9 10:00 AM PST for procurement alignment — let me know if that works.

Thanks,
